newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens flat on quiet overnight trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens flat on quiet overnight trade.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened flat at C$1.3878 (US$0.7205) in light trading on Tuesday after the unit was sidelined in overnight trading on overseas markets, traders said. * They said the Canada dollar traded in a tight range as markets focused on remarks by Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto suggesting a possible sell-off of Japan's U.S treasury holdings.

"I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation to sell off Treasury bills and switch our funds to gold," Hashimoto said.
Japan's Ministry of Finance later said that Hashimoto's comments had been incorrectly reported, but not before the U.S. dollar stumbled to near 114 Japanese yen.

The Canadian dollar, however, escaped any yen-driven downdraft. "The big story was obviously Hashimoto's comments, which didn't involve the Canadian dollar," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.
"It was mostly a U.S. story and an equity story. The treasuries and the bullion did move, but the big hit was on the equity front.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell almost 200 points on Monday in its biggest point drop since the crash of 1987. The Toronto Stock Exchange 300-share composite index lost 73.72 points

Analysts said the Canadian dollar would likely continue trading within a narrow range of C$1.3850 (US$0.7220) and C$1.3900 (US$0.7194) ahead of U.S. data on consumer confidence due to be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
Farrill said that it was uncertain what direction the Canadian dollar would take in the short term.

"The emphasis is going to remain on Canada-U.S. spreads. It's hard to imagine why anyone would want to get overly bullish on the Canada when you're picking up yield in the U.S. with much less sovereign risk," Farrill added.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar was flat at 82.56 yen from Monday's 82.55 yen and climbed to 1.2408 marks from Monday's 1.2363 marks.
